page: Microsoft Azure D48s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable. The processor architecture is x86_64, incorporating advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance across multiple domains. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core metrics fall into the strong category, alongside software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read-only bandwidth is strong, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier. Database operations, including Redis SET operations and PassMark database tests, consistently rank in the top 25%.

The absence of bundled local storage and dedicated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data and limiting its utility for heavy graphics processing. However, the inclusion of AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based machine learning, as evidenced by top 25% scores in prompt processing for small and medium language models. Given its balanced resource density and high-frequency Intel Xeon processor, the D48s_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial compute capacity without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. It is suitable for software compilation, database hosting, web serving, and CPU-driven inference tasks.
